### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TargetFramework condition is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 10

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation for single-TFM projects. The SDK sets it later, after props import. This condition will **never match**, so documentation XML files are silently never generated.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, where `$(TargetFramework)` is resolved:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Unconditional property overrides project settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. This unconditionally overwrites any project-level attempt to set these properties. `LibB` explicitly sets `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (line 13) but it has **no effect** — the `.targets` file stomps it.

**Fix:** Use conditional defaults in `Directory.Build.props` instead (where projects can override):
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA.csproj` — DefineConstants overwrites instead of appending
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing constants (including `TRACE` and `DEBUG` set by the SDK). Code relying on `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:** Append to existing constants:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Unquoted Condition value
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition lacks single-quote wrapping. If `Configuration` is empty, MSBuild evaluates `== Debug` which produces an evaluation error. Additionally, the string comparison without quotes is fragile.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Incorrect F# file compilation order
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, **file order is the compilation order**. `Services.fs` references `BrokenOrder.Domain` (`open BrokenOrder.Domain`), but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This **will cause a compilation error** — the compiler won't find the `Domain` module when compiling `Services.fs`.

**Fix:** `Domain.fs` must come before `Services.fs`:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

### 6. `LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath to packages folder
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–29

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a legacy `packages.config`-style reference. It bypasses NuGet restore, won't get transitive dependency resolution, and the `net6.0` library variant is incorrect for a `net8.0` project.

**Fix:** Convert to PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7, `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

The `.sln` only references LibA and LibB. The `fsharp/` projects aren't part of the solution. If these are meant to be built together, add them to the solution.

Two projects + `Directory.Build.props` all reference packages with inline versions. For consistency and version alignment, consider enabling Central Package Management with a `Directory.Packages.props`.
